chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqoub who said:
I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) cutting the leek by its roots, so he washed it with water and ate it.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams prepare and eat leeks according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* provides a practical legal precedent (sunna) for the permissibility of consuming leeks (kurrath), specifically addressing the fiqh of whether the roots should be retained or discarded. The Imam’s method of washing the entire vegetable, including the roots, with water underscores the principle of general purity (taharah) of plant foods in Shia jurisprudence, countering views that might require peeling or discarding the root end. It serves as a clear example of the Imam’s engagement with daily dietary habits, reinforcing the ease and accessibility of permissible foods in Islamic law.
